headline: Approved final subdivision permits for Grandview Ave and 375 Pushaw Road developments.
summary: The board reviewed and approved a Major Final Subdivision Land Development Permit for a 62-unit development on Grandview Ave, Map-Lot R41-023-A, with conditions on wetland deed restrictions, environmental permitting, trail construction, and deed recording. The board also approved a Major Final Subdivision Land Development Permit for a 22-lot cluster subdivision at 375 Pushaw Road, Map-Lot R30-006-D, with conditions on fire pond maintenance, construction standards, and deed restrictions. Staff also gave an update on zoning map changes as part of ongoing land use plan updates.
decisions: Found that the Grandview Ave application was complete, fees were paid, and the project is a Final Subdivision.
Found the Grandview Ave applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-128G(1) final plat content requirements.
Found the Grandview Ave applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-128G(2) requirements on required plat changes.
Found the Grandview Ave applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-128G(3) City Engineer review requirement.
Found the Grandview Ave applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-128G(4) preliminary plat standards requirement.
Found the Grandview Ave plan was not substantively changed from the preliminary subdivision plat, satisfying §165-128G(5).
Granted the Land Development Permit for the Grandview Ave Major Final Subdivision with conditions on wetland setbacks, environmental permitting, trail construction, and deed recording.
Found the 375 Pushaw Road applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-128G(1) final plat content requirements.
Found the 375 Pushaw Road applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-128G(3) City Engineer review requirement.
Found the 375 Pushaw Road plan met preliminary plat standards and was not substantively changed, satisfying §165-128G(4) and (5).
Granted the Land Development Permit for the 375 Pushaw Road Major Final Subdivision with conditions on fire pond maintenance, construction standards, and deed restrictions.

73 HARLOW STREET, BANGOR, ME  04401 
TELEPHONE: (207) 992-4280          FAX:  (207) 945-4447 
WWW.BANGORMAINE.GOV 
PLANNING BOARD  
TUESDAY, AUGUST 18, 2026, 7:00 P.M. 
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, 1ST FLOOR OF CITY HALL 
73 HARLOW STREET 
 
MEETING MINUTES 
 
  Board Members Present:  Chair Jonathan Boucher 
Vice Chair Janet Jonas  
Ted Brush 
Trisha Hayes 
Ken Huhn (via Zoom) 
Greg Hobson 
Ross Whitford 
 
      
City Staff Present:   Anja Collette, Planning Officer  
        Matt Altiero, Planning Analyst 
Grace Innis, Assistant City Solicitor 
Jefferson Davis, Engineering Director 
 
 
Chair Boucher called the meeting to order at 7:00 P.M.  
 
OLD BUSINESS 
1. Meeting Minutes – August 4, 2026 
Member Brush moved to approve the minutes of August 4, 2026. Seconded by Vice Chair Jonas. Roll call vote 
conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
NEW BUSINESS 
1. Land Development Permit Application – Major Final Subdivision – Grandview Ave 
– Map-Lot R41-023-A – Developers Collaborative Predevelopment LLC –  Land 
Development Permit Application – Major Final Subdivision for a multiphase development 
of 62 residential units. Phase 1 will include the construction of 14 single-family units on a 
proposed residential street and Phase 2 will include the construction of two 24-unit 
multifamily buildings with associated parking. The project is located on Grandview Ave, 
Map-Lot R41-023-A, in the Multifamily and Service District (M&SD). Applicant: 
Developers Collaborative Predevelopment LLC. Owner: City of Bangor. 
 
Chair Boucher introduced the agenda item.
P a g e  2 | 5 
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, August 18, 2026 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that the application was deemed complete on August 18, 2026, all applicable 
fees for the Project have been paid, and the proposed Project is a Final Subdivision. Seconded by 
Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Applicant Representatives Stephen Bushey and Michael Lyne presented on the project, discussing that 
there had been minimal changes since the previous presentation to the Board.  
 
Planning Officer Collette discussed the conditions, explaining that some have remained from preliminary 
approval and are to be completed closer to construction. She shared the additional condition requiring 
completion of the trail prior to the final Certificate of Occupancy being issued. Collette discussed that the 
Open Space Deed and Easement Deeds need to be approved by the City and the Bangor Water District, 
executed, and recorded at the Registry of Deeds prior to building permit issuance. 
 
Chair Boucher asked if there is a signage requirement for the trail – Planning Officer Collette responded 
no. Boucher asked if the trail connects to Brown Woods – Planning Officer Collette responded that the 
trail is across the street from Prentiss Woods. The trail will connect to a parcel owned by Broadway 
Shopping Center, where it then connects to a short path to Hannaford. 
 
Chair Boucher opened public comment – there were none. Public comment closed. 
 
Chair Boucher asked the Board for comments or questions – there were none. 
 
Member Brush moved that the Board finds that based on Exhibit 2, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-128G(1)’s requirements by providing a final plat for a major subdivision with 
the necessary contents of §165-128E(4). Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted – all 
voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hobson moved that the Board finds that based on Exhibit 2, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development §165-128G(2)’s requirements that the final plat contain all the changes or modifications 
required by the Planning Board. Seconded by Member Hayes. Roll call vote conducted – all voting 
members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that based on Exhibits 13 and 14, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-128G(3)’s requirement for the plan to be reviewed by the City Engineer for 
compliance with health, sanitation and engineering standards, and for receiving written approval from the 
City Engineer. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none 
opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Brush moved that the Board finds that based on Exhibits 2 and 15, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-128G(4)’s requirement for meeting the standards for preliminary plat approval. 
Seconded by Vice Chair Jonas. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed. 
 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that Board finds that based on Exhibits 2 and 15, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-128G(5)’s requirement that the plan not be substantively changed from the 
preliminary subdivision plat Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members 
in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.
P a g e  3 | 5 
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, August 18, 2026 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that the Board finds that the Project meets the requirements for a Land 
Development Permit for a Major Final Subdivision and therefore, the Board grants the Land Development 
Permit for the proposed Project, with the following conditions:  
 Deed restrictions are created for lots 1-6 and lot 8 to minimize disturbance within the 75’ setback 
from wetlands of special significance, outside of that required for home construction. 
 Before building permits are issued, the Project receives wetland permitting approval from the 
Maine Department of Environmental Protection and Army Corps of Engineers, including 
permitting for activity within the 75’ setback from wetlands of special significance. 
 The trail shown on the plan will be constructed prior to the final Certificate of Occupancy (CO) 
being issued. 
 The open space deed and easement deeds will be approved by the appropriate City departments 
and the Bangor Water District, executed, and recorded at the Registry of Deeds prior to any 
building permits being issued. 
 
Chair Boucher asked if the Applicant agrees to these conditions – Applicant Representative Lyne 
confirmed. 
 
Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed. 
 
 
2. Land Development Permit – Major Final Subdivision – 375 Pushaw Road – Map-Lot 
R30-006-D –  Land Development Permit Application – Major Final Subdivision for the 
creation of a cluster subdivision of 22 lots located at 375 Pushaw Road, Map-Lot R30-
006-D, in the Rural Residence and Agricultural District (RR&A). Applicant/Owner: T&T 
Property Management, LLC 
Chair Boucher introduced the agenda item. 
 
Member Hobson moved that the application was deemed complete on August 18, 2026, the applicant 
paid all applicable fees, and the proposed Project is a Final Major Subdivision. 
 
Applicant Representative Jim Kiser presented to the podium. 
 
Planning Officer Collette discussed that the fire pond maintenance request will be brought to City Council 
in September, and staff recommends City maintenance of the fire pond. She discussed the condition that 
if City Council rejects maintenance, the applicant would revise the Open Space Deed, and that the fire 
pond must be built to National Fire Protection Association standards. Collette described that the deeds 
for each lot are to include restrictions that buffer areas will be allowed to revert to a natural, undisturbed 
state.  
 
Chair Boucher asked the Board for questions.
P a g e  4 | 5 
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, August 18, 2026 
Chair Boucher asked if additional conditional language is needed in the case that the City accepts 
maintenance of the fire pond – Planning Officer Collette responded no, as the Open Space Deed currently 
reflects City maintenance. 
 
Chair Boucher opened public comment – there were none. Public comment closed. 
 
Member Brush moved that the Board finds that based on Exhibit 2, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-128G(1)’s requirements by providing a final plat for a major subdivision with 
the necessary contents of §165-128E(4). Seconded by Member Hayes. Roll call vote conducted – all 
voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hobson moved that the Board finds that based on Exhibit 22, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-128G(3)’s requirement for the plan to be reviewed by the City Engineer for 
compliance with health, sanitation and engineering standards, and for receiving written approval from the 
City Engineer. Seconded by Member Whitford. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, 
none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hayes moved that the Board finds that based on Exhibits 2 and 24, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-128G(4)’s requirement for meeting the standards for preliminary plat approval 
and §165-128G(5)’s requirement that the plan not be substantively changed from the preliminary 
subdivision plat. Seconded by Vice Chair Jonas. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, 
none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that the Board finds that the project meets the requirements for a Final Major 
Subdivision and therefore, the Board grants the Land Development Permit for the proposed Project, with 
the following conditions: 
 If the City Council rejects maintenance of the fire pond, the open space deed will be revised to 
reflect that T&T Property Management, LLC is responsible for maintenance, and the consent 
agreement that was provided in the original project submissions detailing that T&T Property 
Management, LLC will maintain the fire pond will need to be approved by the City Legal 
Department, executed, and recorded at the Registry of Deeds before any building permits are 
issued. 
 The fire pond will be built to NFPA standards and will be inspected and approved by the City Fire 
Department prior to any building permits being issued. 
 The open space and stormwater easement deeds will be executed, and the deeds and subdivision 
plan will be recorded at the Registry of Deeds prior to any building permit being issued. 
 The deeds for each lot in the subdivision, as applicable, will contain restrictions that the buffer 
areas shown on the subdivision plan will be allowed to revert to a natural, undisturbed state. 
 The letter of credit dated July 2, 2026 from Bangor Savings Bank will be signed by the Vice 
President of Bangor Savings Bank or their designee before any building permit is issued. 
 
Seconded by Member Hobson.  Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed. 
 
OTHER BUSINESS
P a g e  5 | 5 
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, August 18, 2026 
1. Follow-Up/Thoughts on Land Use Plan Updates 
 
Planning Officer Collette provided updates, sharing that she is reviewing zoning map changes. She discussed 
that sessions are scheduled with the consultants at the end of the month and in early September to review 
comments. 
 
Meeting adjourned at 7:44 PM. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Kayleigh Rienas 
Development Assistant 
Planning Division
